Zaalkerk uit 1950 van J. Deltrap, sinds: Hall church from 1950 by J. Deltrap, homes since 2024
Neoclassicistisch zaalkerkje met dakruit: Neoclassical hall church with a roof turret, national monument
Dorpsschool met zes lokalen uit ca. 1930: Village school with six classrooms from c. 1930
Kop-rompboerderij uit 1913, rijksmonumen: Head-and-body farmhouse from 1913, national monument, now an ice cream farm
Hotel en eetcafé midden in het dorp, teg: Hotel and café in the middle of the village, opposite the church.
Een van de grote tabaksschuren aan de Ge: One of the large tobacco barns on the Geldersestraat, then still called the Geldersche Laan. For a while the name Waldeck-Hoeve was painted on the side wall; now it is two houses. On the map of 1889 the land around it is yellow with tobacco fields.
Schuin tegenover de Waldeck-Hoeve staat: Diagonally across from the Waldeck-Hoeve stands the next large tobacco barn of the Geldersestraat, from the days when tobacco was grown here.
Zanger, pianist en liedjesschrijver Jule: Singer, pianist and songwriter Jules de Corte (1924-1996) lived here from 1973 until his death, often working on his songs late into the night. He wrote more than 4,000 of them, among them Ik zou wel eens willen weten and Koning Onbenul.
Martinus van de Mortel, Tinus de Fauts,: Martinus van de Mortel, known as Tinus de Fauts, started a small butter factory here, De Fuke. It did not pay well enough and soon closed again. The building still stands and is now a house.
In 1910 bouwde de Maatschappij twee koni: In 1910 the Maatschappij Helenaveen built two royal farms that are almost each other's double: the Emmahoeve and this Julianahoeve, finished in 1911. The first tenant was Johannes Dekker from North Holland. Today it is Landgoed Julianahoeve, with a campsite.
De Julianahoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voo: The Julianahoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
De Maatschappij Helenaveen bouwde deze k: The Maatschappij Helenaveen built this royal farm in 1912, on the Helenavaart by the drained Soemeer lake, where a house already stood in 1889. Today it is a group accommodation.
De Oranjehoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voor: The Oranjehoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
Tot 1982 was dit de openbare lagere scho: Until 1982 this was the public primary school De Zonnedauw, which came when the village's other school became Catholic. Since 21 May 1983 it has been the youth centre De Wiek, named after the wieken: the side branches of the peat canals where turf boats could turn or moor. On the front is a ceramic relief by Frans Jacobs, an artist from Deurne, made at De Porceleyne Fles.
Een betonnen kazemat van de Peel-Raamste: A concrete casemate of the Peel-Raam Line, of the type called a porcupine. Three of them stood on this side of the canal, between the Protestant church and the Geldersestraat, manned by soldiers of the 30th Infantry Regiment. Only number 206 is still there.
De snackbar van het dorp: friet om mee t: The village snack bar: chips to take away, or on the terrace.
Tankstation aan de A67, met een Spar exp: Petrol station on the A67, with a Spar express.
Voor de inwoners die door deportatie of: For the villagers who died through deportation or acts of war, unveiled on 4 May 1985. Two low walls stand for the foundations of the village, which came through the war; against them rests a triangular stone like a roof, with 22 names.
Beeld: de jager die het zwijn doodde: Statue: the hunter who killed the boar
Op het grasveld naast de kerk hangt een: On the lawn next to the church hangs a carillon of 23 bells by Eijsbouts of Asten, paid for by the King William III Fund. At the opening on 6 December 1975 Jules de Corte accompanied the village children in Hertog Jan: his debut as a carillon player. Since 1996 the carillon has carried his name, with his line on a bronze plate: In de oude toren zingt het carillon (in the old tower the carillon sings).
Stalen balken in rood, blauw en geel, va: Steel beams in red, blue and yellow by Norbert Veeger, an artist from Breda. Mayor Van Genabeek unveiled it on 23 January 1990.
Op de vindplaats van de Gouden Helm, die: On the spot where the Golden Helmet came out of the peat in 1910. Joep Coppens made the little temple of basalt lava, bronze and brick. Its front reads E PALUDE EMERGO: I rose up out of the bog.
Voor de 21 mannen die tussen 1940 en 195: For the 21 men who died between 1940 and 1954 in five plane crashes in the Peel. The monument puts names to victims who long stayed anonymous. An initiative of Piet Snellen and Sjaar Huijs, designed by Ruud van der Beele and unveiled in October 2021.
Voor de kerkrazzia van 8 oktober 1944. U: For the church raid of 8 October 1944. 143 people were taken away from Helenaveen; 26 men did not survive the war. It belongs to a series placed in 45 villages between the Maas and the Peel in 2004; blacksmith Thijs van de Manakker made the wrought-iron stand.
Hier stond een Koningswoning, in 1888 ge: A King's house stood here, built in 1888 with a gift from King William III and destroyed in 1921 by a great peat fire. At the initiative of Jan van Woezik the old house pit was dug out again, with the Hellhound by Helenaveen artist Dirk Verberne.
Op 19 mei 1945 ruimden Frans van den Eij: On 19 May 1945 Frans van den Eijnden from Liessel and corporal Meindert Postma from Drachten were clearing mines here, where the Lagebrugweg and the Oude Peelstraat meet. A bouncing mine went off and both were killed.
In 1861 stelde de Maatschappij hier, op: In 1861 the Maatschappij made a small building available here, on the corner of the Geldersestraat and the Jan Deckersstraat, as the first school. Across the road lay the shipyard. It was only a stopgap: a new school soon followed.
Aan de Fruitweg werd in 1857 een katholi: In 1857 a Catholic makeshift church was set up on the Fruitweg in the converted stable of a farm. Next to it lay the first graveyard of Helenaveen, about 20 by 25 metres, where 35 people were buried.
Jan en Nicolaas van de Griendt kopen hie: Jan and Nicolaas van de Griendt buy 610 hectares of raised bog here, to dig out the peat and then turn the land into farmland. The village that grows up in the south-east corner they name after Helena, Jan's wife.
Helena Panis, de vrouw van Jan van de Gr: Helena Panis, the wife of Jan van de Griendt, after whom the village is named (public domain)
Een borstbeeld van koningin Juliana door: A bust of Queen Juliana by Jesualda Kwanten, on the Dominee Swaluestraat. The royal family has long been connected with Helenaveen, through the King William III Fund and the royal farms.
Borstbeeld van koningin Juliana, WoodenS: Bust of Queen Juliana, WoodenSpoon, CC BY-SA 4.0
Om de turf af te voeren laat Van de Grie: To carry off the peat, Van de Griendt has his own canal dug, from the Noordervaart near Meijel into the Peel. The digging starts in June 1853; in January 1854 the canal diggers reach the site of the village. They come from everywhere: from the surrounding area, from the peat colonies in the north, and as seasonal workers from around Hanover.
De Helenavaart in 1957, Nationaal Archie: The Helenavaart in 1957, Nationaal Archief, Nederlandse Heidemaatschappij (CC0)
De Helenavaart tussen Griendtsveen en He: The Helenavaart between Griendtsveen and Helenaveen, 2010 (public domain)
Een eenvoudig neoclassicistisch zaalkerk: A simple neoclassical hall church for the Protestant peat workers, with a pediment and a roof turret on the front. In 1883 the front got a memorial stone when the minister Swalue died. It is a national monument.
Protestantse kerk in 1979, Rijksdienst v: The Protestant church in 1979, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
Dominee E.B. Swalue, predikant in Helena: Reverend E.B. Swalue, minister in Helenaveen from 1867 to 1883 (public domain)
Het interieur in 2013, Peter Bankers, CC: The interior in 2013, Peter Bankers, CC BY-SA 4.0
De predikantenwoning, Soemeersingel 25,: The minister's house, Soemeersingel 25, is as old as the church next to it. In the front garden stands an S-casemate, a small bunker of the Peel-Raam Line. In May 1940 there was fighting in Helenaveen.
De pastorie in 1979, Rijksdienst voor he: The parsonage in 1979, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
Rechts tegen de kerk kwam rond 1880 een: Against the right side of the church a Sunday school was built around 1880, and rebuilt in 1900. Together with the church and the parsonage it forms the Protestant complex on the Helenavaart.
Kerk, zondagsschool en pastorie vanaf de: Church, Sunday school and parsonage from across the canal, 1997, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
De bovenste, lichte laag veen, het grauw: The top, light layer of peat, the grey peat, burned badly and was at first simply thrown back. When people found it made good bedding for stables, the Maatschappij Helenaveen built a peat litter factory here, with houses for the staff against it. The national monument on the Rector Nuijtsstraat was lost in a large fire on 4 May 2025.
De voormalige fabriek met de dienstwonin: The former factory with the staff houses, 2013, John Scholte, CC BY-SA 3.0 NL
Een kleine boerderij met een schuurtje e: A small farm with a shed and a cart barn, Soemeersingel 75. This is how the smallholders lived who worked a few hectares of land next to their work in the peat, a world apart from the large royal farms further on.
Het Wehrmachthuisje aan de Koolweg: The Wehrmacht hut on the Koolweg
Tegen de bosrand aan de Koolweg bouwden: Against the edge of the woods on the Koolweg the Germans built a hut for the crew of a searchlight. It was part of the Kammhuber Line, the air defence against British bombers on their way to the Ruhr. It stands behind Koolweg 42 against the edge of the woods, at number 40 I think.
De eerste van elf grote boerderijen die: The first of eleven large farms that the Maatschappij Helenaveen built from 1908 on, under director Adrianus Bos. They are called royal farms after members of the royal family; that the King William III Fund built them is a misconception, it only contributed to a few of them.
De Wilhelminahoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst: The Wilhelminahoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
De Nassauhoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voor: The Nassauhoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
De Hendrikhoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voo: The Hendrikhoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
Aan de Soemeersingel, bij de Willem III-: On the Soemeersingel, near the Willem III-hoeve, stands Peeltroef by Dirk Verberne: two peat benches and a column that shows how high the peat stood here before it was dug away.
Peeltroef van Dirk Verberne, WoodenSpoon: Peeltroef by Dirk Verberne, WoodenSpoon, CC BY-SA 4.0
De noordelijkste koningshoeve, met het j: The northernmost royal farm, with the year and the name in its stepped gable. A national monument, and today an ice cream farm with a terrace.
De Willem III-hoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst: The Willem III-hoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
De Willem III-hoeve in 1997, Rijksdienst: The Willem III-hoeve in 1997, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
Nog een van de koningshoeven, aan de Kaa: Another of the royal farms, on the Kaasweg, named after Queen Emma. Like the other farms it is a head-and-body farmhouse: a house with a large barn behind it.
De Emmahoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voor h: The Emmahoeve in 1979, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed, CC BY-SA 4.0
De Emmahoeve met varkensstal, 2013, John: The Emmahoeve with its pigsty, 2013, John Scholte, CC BY-SA 3.0 NL
Het Peelkanaal bij Evertsoord is een rij: The Peelkanaal near Evertsoord is a national monument of the Peel-Raam Line, the defence line of 1939 and 1940. The canal served as a moat against tanks; along the line stood casemates like the one in the parsonage garden.
In 1915 stopt de grote turfwinning en wo: In 1915 the large-scale peat digging stops, and from then on the land is mostly reclaimed for farming and market gardening. What you see here is what is left of the raised bog: heath, fens and woods, now nature in the Deurnsche Peel.
Hoogveen in de Mariapeel bij Helenaveen,: Raised bog in the Mariapeel near Helenaveen, Aat van den Heuvel, CC BY 3.0
Uit Gelderland kwamen tabakstelers naar: Tobacco growers came to Helenaveen from Gelderland. The Maatschappij Helenaveen had a barn built here to dry the tobacco; by around 1880 it was already split into two farms.
De voormalige tabaksschuur in 2021, Sil: The former tobacco barn in 2021, Sil Bouwmans, CC BY-SA 4.0
Na het veen kwam de tuinbouw. Groente gi: After the peat came market gardening. Vegetables first went to Venlo by steam tram; today large greenhouses fill the view east of the village.
In de oorlog ging de rooms-katholieke ke: During the war the Roman Catholic church of 1857 was lost, an early work of the famous architect P.J.H. Cuypers. On 8 October 1944 the Germans held a raid at the church and took men from the village away. The war memorial on the Oude Peelstraat was put up at the initiative of those who came back.
Het oorlogsmonument aan de Oude Peelstra: The war memorial on the Oude Peelstraat, WoodenSpoon, CC BY-SA 4.0
Gedenkteken uit 2004 voor de razzia van: Memorial from 2004 for the raid of 1944, Peter Bankers, CC BY-SA 4.0
Op dezelfde plek bouwde J. Deltrap een n: On the same spot J. Deltrap built a new church: a simple hall church in traditional forms, with a bell tower that rises 26 metres above the village. At the end of 2023 the church was closed with a farewell service; it now holds fourteen homes, and a Lady chapel that stays open for prayer.
De Sint-Willibrorduskerk in 2022, ACABJU: The Sint-Willibrorduskerk in 2022, ACABJULIA, CC BY-SA 4.0
Reliëf van Sint-Willibrord door Frans Tu: Relief of Saint Willibrord by Frans Tuinstra, WoodenSpoon, CC BY-SA 4.0
Na het vervenen moest de grond nog ontgo: Once the peat was dug, the land still had to be reclaimed, from 1937 also by unemployed men on relief work. With tipping carts they built roads, dug ditches and filled in old peat canals. The carts on the Kerkplein recall that; they had nothing to do with cutting peat.
De jager die het zwijn doodde: The hunter who killed the boar
Een beeld van Niel Steenbergen uit 1956,: A statue by Niel Steenbergen from 1956, now a municipal monument: a hunter with the wild boar he has killed.
De jager die het zwijn doodde, WoodenSpo: The hunter who killed the boar, WoodenSpoon, CC BY-SA 4.0
Op de hoek van de Soemeersingel en de Se: On the corner of the Soemeersingel and the Sevenumseweg stands Verleden Veen by Jan Ros, made for 150 years of Helenaveen, which was celebrated in 2003.
Verleden Veen van Jan Ros, WoodenSpoon,: Verleden Veen by Jan Ros, WoodenSpoon, CC BY-SA 4.0
Het dorpshuis draagt de naam van de verg: The village hall carries the name of the gilded Roman helmet that was found in the peat near Helenaveen in 1910.
Een gaaf bewaarde dorpsschool met zes lo: A well-preserved village school with six classrooms and a small bell tower on the roof. Still the primary school of Helenaveen.
Op het katholieke kerkhof aan de Aardbei: At the Catholic graveyard on the Aardbeiweg, volunteers of Memori work to keep the old graves, and with them the stories of the people who built the village. There are Dutch war graves too.
Oude graven op de katholieke begraafplaa: Old graves in the Catholic cemetery (public domain)
Aan de Aardbeiweg liggen veenarbeiders b: On the Aardbeiweg lie peat workers who came from far away: from the raised bog areas in the north of the Netherlands and from Germany.
In het veen bij Helenaveen werd in 1910: In 1910 the gilded helmet of a Roman officer was found in the peat near Helenaveen: the Golden Helmet of Deurne. The community centre in the village is named after it; a memorial stands where it was found.
De helm in het Rijksmuseum van Oudheden,: The helmet in the Rijksmuseum van Oudheden, Michiel (Wiki Loves Art), CC BY-SA 2.0
Vanwege de bijzondere geschiedenis als v: Because of its special history as a peat colony, Helenaveen has been a protected village since 1999. This is the end of the tour. Many more stories, photos and maps are on Het Helenaveen van toen (in Dutch).
